source.name: Mapzen / Tilezen Terrain Tiles (Terrarium) on AWS Open Data
source.license: Multisource open terrain data; source-specific terms and attribution are documented by Tilezen. Global SRTM and GMTED2010 data are public domain. OSM peak data is ODbL 1.0.
source.attribution: Terrain: Mapzen; SRTM and GMTED2010 terrain data courtesy of the U.S. Geological Survey; ETOPO1 terrain data courtesy of NOAA. Peak locations: © OpenStreetMap contributors.
source.gridConvention: Flat row-major heights in meters: north-to-south rows, west-to-east columns. Grid nodes include both bounding edges; EPSG:4326 bounds.
source.resampling: Bilinear from RGB Terrarium tiles in Web Mercator, zoom 11; R*256+G+B/256-32768. Output rounded to 0.1 m without terrain alteration.
notes: These are real regional DEM heights, not invented mountain silhouettes. Source tile HTTP Last-Modified dates are 2017-11-20; underlying elevation observations may be older.
The 128 by 128 output covers about 36.4 km east-west by 33.4 km north-south. Grid spacing is about 286 m east-west and 263 m north-south; peaks and narrow ridges are smoothed.
Peak label elevations are independent OSM metadata, not replacements for the terrain grid. No height adjustment has been made to force DEM samples to match summit labels.
Regional DEM does not resolve buildings, bridge decks, lanes, road grades, retaining walls, or current construction. Vertical datum was not independently verified for these individual tiles.
Game rendering may subtract a local height baseline or flatten the immediate road corridor. Those changes are visual/driving approximations and are not stored in this source grid.
The exact DEM source contributing each pixel has not been independently traced; general terrain attribution is retained rather than claiming exclusive SRTM provenance.
